correctness.rationale: The mathematical statement is correct. The identity element is adjacent to every vertex, hence the full enhanced power graph has diameter at most two. If the group has at least four elements, the identity has degree at least three and the graph is not a path; for order three the group is cyclic and the graph is K_3. The cited diameter-two theorem then gives infinite multiset dimension. Orders one and two give P_1 and P_2, whose multiset dimension is one under the cited convention. The packaged finite examples agree, but the proof is entirely analytic.

originality.rationale: Originality fails under the implication standard. Simanjuntak--Siagian--Vetrik already prove the stronger graph-theoretic theorem that every non-path graph of diameter at most two has infinite multiset dimension, and that multiset dimension one is exactly the path case. In every full enhanced power graph the identity is visibly universal from the definition, so the graph has diameter at most two. The remaining order-three and smaller cases are immediate. Thus the claimed classification is a direct corollary of a prior general theorem plus the defining identity-vertex observation, even though the 2022 survey later posed the family-specific question explicitly.
